summary: Recorded the trim finding and bounded the runtime defect's condition. The trim execution (CheckRun fe11b982193b4d7c811c9572ec41b223, exit 0) evaluated both comparisons completely — control {1,2,3} `holds` (trim(None) moved the compacted index 0→1 with every server decided) and treatment {1,2,5} `violated` with valid witness index 3 (trim(None) returned `ok` while the compacted index stayed 0, and the documented repair `trim(Some(1))` returned `NotAllDecided(0)`) — so I appended the account as a scoped progress/availability defect (trim silently no-ops, the documented retry cannot succeed, snapshotting is the only remaining compaction path, decision counting is unaffected), promoted the behaviour to knowledge, and noted the source-derived generalisation that any id set with a phantom slot below the largest id triggers it. For the runtime question I built a tick-period sweep (validated locally: with a ~2 ms re-sync round trip the false success appears at 8, 16, 40 and 80 ms and the documented Superseded arm at 2 and 4 ms — the crate's default tick period is 10 ms) and submitted it as the fixed experiment, with a derived boolean whose operands stay visible so one uniform predicate covers all seven cases. Incomplete: the sweep receipt is pending, and the follower-origin variant remains the only unmeasured item on the runtime question.
